content:
ken: Heads up — billing/usage alert: a customer reported ~2x token charges for an interactive stream when the client retried the toolcall after a websocket disconnect. Repro steps and logs below.

alia: ugh. do we have an incident id or sample trace?

ken: trace id: trace-7f9c ; stream session: s_42f3. snippet from proxy logs: 
```
[2025-05-04T16:21:03Z] session s_42f3: client.open
[2025-05-04T16:21:09Z] request r_9a: start stream, model=gpt-open-22, prompt-prefix="User: ..."
[2025-05-04T16:21:12Z] response chunk token_count=14, sequence=1
[2025-05-04T16:21:14Z] network: reset by peer
[2025-05-04T16:21:15Z] client retry r_9a (new websocket), idempotency=none
[2025-05-04T16:21:16Z] backend accepted second start, generated same 14 tokens -> billed twice
```

sara: was there any toolcall in the middle? toolcall could be the culprit if TTL didn't expire.

ken: yes — there was a toolcall to the retrieval service at sequence=1 (single call). toolcall id t_77. backend logs show it executed twice.

robin: so two separate generator runs + same toolcall run. question: who should own dedupe? router/proxy, or runtime?

alia: quick note: we already dedupe non-streaming requests by idempotency key, but streaming start/stop + interleaved toolcalls are messy. The client retried the websocket not the original HTTP start, so no idempotency token was sent.

ken: right. customer client is a mobile app that reopens a stream on transient network errors; they didn't persist idempotency tokens.

alia: proposal A: server assigns a short-lived stream token on first start and returns it in headers. If a reconnect happens within Xs and includes the token, we treat as same session and avoid double billing for overlapping token output.

robin: That helps for reconnects, but doesn't work if the original stream request actually completed on the backend and generated output that the client never acknowledged. We still need a definition of "charged tokens" vs "delivered tokens". Billing wants consistency.

billing-bot: FYI from billing team: our current rule is "bill on generator accept". Changing that is non-trivial but possible. We can consider billing credits for dedup on a per-customer basis.

alia: alternative B: server-side dedupe window keyed by (session fingerprint, prompt-prefix-hash, toolcall-seq). If two accepted generator runs have identical fingerprint and overlap in produced token sequence within Yms, we mark second as duplicate and do not bill. This needs KV storage and race handling.

ken: can we approximate with deterministic output hash? e.g., hash of first N tokens. But streaming outputs may be nondeterministic across runs (sampling). In our reproducible-serving tests many runs differ slightly, so exact-match dedupe will undercount.

robin: idea C: attribute partial credit. If the second run replays tokens 1..14 identical, mark those tokens as duplicate and only bill unique suffix. That requires per-token diffing at accounting layer and aligning streams by sequence numbers — messy but precise.

alia: also toolcalls: we need to avoid double-charging toolcalls invoked by the model (toolcall billing). If model calls a retrieval tool twice because of retry, tool operator may bill separately. We should emit toolcall idempotency tokens to tool providers.

sara: operational ask: can we detect these events and auto-issue credits while we design a long-term fix? We have customer upset already.

billing-bot: we can run a script to reconcile duplicates based on trace ids and token counts, but it's manual and will take days. Provide a list of affected traces.

ken: I exported the traces: trace-7f9c, trace-7f9d, trace-7faa, plus a set of ~12 similar across that customer. I'll drop in #support.

robin: short-term engineering mitigation: enforce server idempotency token on stream start for all SDKs (0.8) and return an explicit header X-Stream-Id. Client SDKs must persist across reconnects. That should cut new occurrences by 90%.

alia: plus add a cheap server check: if an identical generator run arrives within 5s and session fingerprint matches, return status 409 with guidance to reconnect to existing stream instead of starting new generation. No backend re-exec.

ken: is 409 safe? existing clients may treat as fatal. Maybe return 200 with a header "x-duplicate: true" and empty body. But that might confuse streaming flows.

robin: prefer 409 with JSON error and clear client SDK handling. Update SDKs to auto-reconnect. We'll add fallback to force idempotency token generation when not provided.

alia: action items:
- ken: file a postmortem with affected traces + customer impact (ASAP)
- robin: design idempotency token handshake + 5s dedupe behavior (PR by EOD tomorrow)
- sara: coordinate with billing to create priority credits for the customer
- billing-bot: run manual reconciliation script once ken uploads traces

deploy-bot: deploy queued: proxy:stream-session-reject-409 -> canary 20% in us-west (build b-554)

ken: thanks. I'll ping the customer and mark them as handled. We'll follow up with an RFC for long-term accounting model (deliver vs accept). :thumbsup:

alia: small note for the RFC: include edge case about truncation when client cancels mid-stream — we need to decide if cancelled tokens are billable. Current policy: billed on generation acceptance, so yes. That triggers a lot of customer complaints though.

robin: let's capture examples in RFC. Also look at toolcall billing separately — providers may want webhook dedupe support.

sara: I'll set up a Zoom with the customer ops team for tomorrow.

ken: thread closed for now, will reopen if more traces come in.
